Coherent multi-cause forecasts with cause shares (deprecated)

Source: R/model-causes.R
cause_shares.Rd

Deprecated. cause_shares() is a method of this package without a published source (a Tucker4 decomposition of isometric log-ratio coordinates of cause shares). Use reconciled() with a hierarchy of causes (separate models made coherent), or coda_causes(), the multiple-decrement compositional model of Oeppen (2008). cause_shares() still works and warns (class mt_warning_deprecated).

Usage

cause_shares(
  total = lee_carter(),
  var = "cause",
  total_level = "all",
  ranks = c(3, 3, 2, 2),
  residual = "auto",
  residual_noise = TRUE
)

Arguments

total

Model specification for all-cause mortality.

var

Stratum variable with the causes.

total_level

Level of var for all causes.

ranks

Tucker ranks for age, year, group and ILR coordinate.

residual

Add a residual cause so that listed causes may cover less than all deaths: TRUE, FALSE, or "auto" (added when the listed causes leave more than 0.1% of all-cause mortality unexplained in the median cell; a residual that is zero almost everywhere would only add a degenerate coordinate).

residual_noise

Add in-sample residual variation of the ILR coordinates to the draws (in predictive draws split multinomially, the part beyond the multinomial variation).

Value

A model specification.

Details

Forecasts all-cause mortality with any model (total) and the shares of the causes in all-cause mortality with a compositional tensor model, so that cause-specific forecasts add up to the all-cause forecast in every draw:

  1. shares of each cause (and of a residual cause, the part of all-cause mortality not covered by the listed causes) per age, year and group;

  2. isometric log-ratio (ILR) coordinates of the shares (orthonormal Helmert basis);

  3. Tucker decomposition of the array [age, year, group, coordinate] (HOOI) with ranks ranks; the year factors are forecast as a multivariate random walk with drift (bootstrap of joint changes) and the in-sample residual variation is added to the draws;

  4. inverse ILR gives share draws, which multiply the all-cause draws.

Shares of rare causes are noisy; smoothing the rates first (prep = mt_prep(step_smooth())) can help.

Predictive draws (mt_forecast(predictive = TRUE)) are the predictive draws of the total model; for models of expected rates (such as lee_carter()) these are Poisson deaths given the rates (no other observation noise is added), which are split between the causes (and the residual cause) multinomially by the share draws, so that the deaths of the causes add up to the all-cause deaths also in predictive draws. The residual variation of the shares added to these draws is then only the part beyond the multinomial variation. For total models of observed rates (rwd(), arima_series(), ets_series()), predictive draws are the draws.

The data need a stratum variable var with the all-cause level total_level and the cause levels; other stratum variables (for example sex) define the groups.

References

Egozcue JJ, Pawlowsky-Glahn V, Mateu-Figueras G, Barcelo-Vidal C (2003). Isometric logratio transformations for compositional data analysis. Mathematical Geology 35(3): 279-300.

See also

reconciled(), coda_causes().

Examples

x <- mt_example_causes(years = 2010:2019)
fit <- mt_fit(suppressWarnings(cause_shares(total = lee_carter(), ranks = c(2, 2, 2, 2))), x)
fc <- mt_forecast(fit, h = 5, n_draws = 50, seed = 1)
# the replacement:
fit2 <- mt_fit(coda_causes(), x)
